hook_text: Two sixes. One is worth 6 000, the other 60 000. Same digit, different seat.
clip_script: A house in Gqeberha costs R765 430. Six seats from the right: units, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. The 7 sits in the hundred thousands seat: R700 000. The 6 sits in the ten thousands seat: R60 000. Now 136 482 learners writing a test. Here the 6 sits in the thousands seat: only 6 000. One seat to the right, ten times smaller. Break it up: 100 000 plus 30 000 plus 6 000 plus 400 plus 80 plus 2. Build it back and every part goes to its seat. Cards 4, 0, 7, 2, 9, 5. Biggest number: 975 420. Smallest: 204 579, because zero cannot lead. The seat decides the value.
visual_style: A six-seat place value chart with digits hopping between seats and their values growing ten times with each hop.
mood: Playful, like musical chairs with numbers.
pacing: Two sixes compared, a quick break-up and build-back, then the digit card challenge.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make the biggest and smallest numbers from six digit cards of your own.
